bookSections.title: Compare and Order Fractions, Decimals and Percentages

preamble.whatYouWillLearn: You will see that a fraction is really a division, and switch between improper fractions and mixed numbers. You will simplify fractions, change between fractions, decimals and percentages, and find percentages of shapes and amounts. You will put mixed lists of numbers in order, and convert time intervals between decimals and hours and minutes, like 1.75 hours = 1 hour 45 minutes.
preamble.whyItMatters: Fractions, decimals and percentages are three ways of writing the same amount. If you can switch between them quickly, many exam questions become much easier. Time is different: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so 0.5 hours is 30 minutes, not 50.
realWorld: A shop sign says 25% off a pair of RM 80 shoes
Sharing 3 roti canai equally between 4 friends: each gets 3/4 of one
Your phone battery shows 45%, a bit less than half full
Scoring 17 out of 20 on a test is the same as 85%
Knowing a 0.75-hour badminton session is 45 minutes, not 75

subtopics.title: Fractions as division
subtopics.summary: A fraction is a division: 3/4 means 3 ÷ 4. Change between improper fractions and mixed numbers.

subtopics.title: Equivalent fractions and simplest form
subtopics.summary: Multiply or divide the numerator and denominator by the same number to make equivalent fractions. Divide by the highest common factor to simplify.

subtopics.title: Fractions, decimals and percentages
subtopics.summary: Change between the three forms, for example 1/4 = 0.25 = 25%.

subtopics.title: Percentages of shapes and amounts
subtopics.summary: Find what percentage of a shape is shaded, and work out percentages of whole numbers, such as 35% of 80.

subtopics.title: Comparing and ordering
subtopics.summary: Compare and order fractions, decimals and percentages by changing them into the same form, and use the symbols <, > and =.

subtopics.title: Time as decimals and mixed units
subtopics.summary: Convert time between decimal hours and hours and minutes, for example 1.75 h = 1 h 45 min and 0.2 h = 12 min.

questions.prompt: Which fraction means the same as 3 ÷ 4?
questions.solution: A fraction is a division: the numerator is divided by the denominator. So 3 ÷ 4 is written as 3/4. (It is equal to 0.75.)

misconceptions.1: This is 4 ÷ 3, the wrong way round. The number being divided (3) goes on top, and the number you divide by (4) goes on the bottom.
misconceptions.2: The ÷ sign is not a decimal point. 3 shared between 4 gives each less than 1 whole, so the answer must be less than 1.
misconceptions.3: This is 3 x 4. Dividing is not the same as multiplying: 3 ÷ 4 is less than 1.

questions.prompt: Work out 7 ÷ 2. Give your answer as a decimal or a mixed number.
questions.solution: 7 ÷ 2 = 3 remainder 1. The remainder 1 still has to be shared by 2, which gives 1/2. So 7 ÷ 2 = 3 1/2 = 3.5. Well done if you got it!

misconceptions.common: Writing 3 r 1 as 3.1. The remainder 1 is 1 out of 2, which is 1/2 = 0.5, not 0.1.

questions.prompt: Write 2 1/3 as an improper fraction.
questions.solution: Each whole is 3 thirds, so 2 wholes = 2 x 3 = 6 thirds. Add the extra 1 third: 6 + 1 = 7 thirds. So 2 1/3 = 7/3.

misconceptions.0: You changed the 2 wholes into 6 thirds, but forgot to add the extra 1/3. 6/3 + 1/3 = 7/3.
misconceptions.2: You added the whole number to the denominator (2 + 3 = 5). Instead, multiply the whole number by the denominator, then add the numerator: 2 x 3 + 1 = 7.
misconceptions.3: The fraction is upside down. We are counting thirds, so the denominator stays 3.

questions.prompt: Write 17/5 as a mixed number.
questions.solution: 17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2. So there are 3 wholes and 2 fifths left over: 17/5 = 3 2/5.

misconceptions.common: Writing 3 2/17 or 3 5/2. The pieces are still fifths, so the denominator stays 5, and the remainder (2) becomes the numerator.

questions.prompt: 6 pizzas are shared equally between 8 children. How much pizza does each child get?
questions.solution: Sharing means dividing: 6 ÷ 8 = 6/8. Simplify by dividing top and bottom by 2: 6/8 = 3/4. Each child gets 3/4 of a pizza. Check: there are fewer pizzas than children, so each child gets less than a whole one.

misconceptions.0: This is 8 ÷ 6, the wrong way round. We share the pizzas (6) between the children (8), so it is 6 ÷ 8. There are fewer pizzas than children, so each child gets less than 1 pizza.
misconceptions.1: Taking away 8 - 6 does not share anything. Sharing equally means dividing: 6 ÷ 8.
misconceptions.3: 1/8 is what each child gets from ONE pizza. There are 6 pizzas, so each child gets 6 of those eighths: 6/8 = 3/4.

questions.prompt: True or false: 9/4 is greater than 2.
questions.solution: 9/4 = 9 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 1, so 9/4 = 2 1/4. That is more than 2, so the statement is true.

misconceptions.common: Thinking that a fraction is always less than 1. When the numerator is bigger than the denominator (an improper fraction), the value is more than 1.

questions.prompt: Match each division to its answer written as a mixed number.
questions.solution: 5 ÷ 2 = 2 r 1 = 2 1/2. 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3 = 1 3/4. 10 ÷ 3 = 3 r 1 = 3 1/3. 9 ÷ 5 = 1 r 4 = 1 4/5. The remainder goes on top and the number you divided by goes on the bottom.

misconceptions.common: Putting the remainder over the wrong number, for example writing 9 ÷ 5 as 1 4/9. The remainder goes over the number you divided by: 9 ÷ 5 = 1 r 4 = 1 4/5.

questions.prompt: Siti pours 15 kg of flour equally into 4 bags. Siti says each bag holds 3 3/4 kg. Wei Ming says each bag holds 3.75 kg. Who is right?
questions.solution: 15 ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 3, so each bag holds 3 3/4 kg. Since 3/4 = 0.75, 3 3/4 kg = 3.75 kg. They wrote the same amount in two different ways, so both are right.

misconceptions.0: Siti is right, but so is Wei Ming: 3/4 = 0.75, so 3.75 kg is the same amount written as a decimal.
misconceptions.1: Wei Ming is right, but so is Siti: 3.75 written as a mixed number is 3 3/4.
misconceptions.2: Perhaps you worked out 15 ÷ 4 = 3 r 3 and wrote it as 3.3. The remainder 3 means 3 quarters, which is 0.75, not 0.3.

questions.prompt: A jug holds 2 3/4 litres of water. How many 1/4-litre cups can it fill exactly?
questions.solution: Each litre is 4 quarters, so 2 litres = 2 x 4 = 8 quarters. Add the extra 3 quarters: 8 + 3 = 11 quarters. So the jug fills 11 cups. (This is the same as 2 3/4 = 11/4.)

misconceptions.common: Getting 8 (counting only the 2 whole litres) or 5 (adding 2 + 3). Change the mixed number into quarters: 2 x 4 + 3 = 11.

questions.prompt: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2?
questions.solution: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number. 1 x 4 = 4 and 2 x 4 = 8, so 1/2 = 4/8. Check: 4 is half of 8.

misconceptions.1: You added 1 to the top and the bottom. Adding does not keep a fraction the same size; multiply (or divide) both numbers by the same number instead.
misconceptions.2: You doubled only the denominator. That makes the pieces smaller, so 1/4 is less than 1/2.
misconceptions.3: You added 4 to the top and the bottom. 5/6 is much more than a half. Multiply both numbers by the same number instead.

questions.prompt: Fill in the missing number: 3/4 = ?/12
questions.solution: 4 x 3 = 12, so the denominator was multiplied by 3. Do the same to the numerator: 3 x 3 = 9. So 3/4 = 9/12.

misconceptions.common: Answering 11 by adding 8 to the top because 4 + 8 = 12. Equivalent fractions come from multiplying, not adding: 4 x 3 = 12, so 3 x 3 = 9.

questions.prompt: Write 6/8 in its simplest form.
questions.solution: 6 and 8 can both be divided by 2: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. 3 and 4 have no common factor except 1, so 3/4 is the simplest form.

misconceptions.0: You halved the numerator but not the denominator. Whatever you do to the top, you must also do to the bottom.
misconceptions.2: 12/16 is equal to 6/8, but the numbers got bigger. Simplest form means the smallest possible numbers, so divide, do not multiply.
misconceptions.3: You took 4 away from the top and the bottom. Taking away changes the size: 2/4 is only a half, but 6/8 is more than a half.

questions.prompt: Select ALL the fractions that are equivalent to 2/3.
questions.solution: 4/6 = 2/3 multiplied by 2 on top and bottom. 6/9 = multiplied by 3. 10/15 = multiplied by 5. The others were made by adding, or by changing only the denominator, so they are not equal to 2/3.

misconceptions.1: 3/4 comes from adding 1 to the top and bottom. Adding does not make equivalent fractions.
misconceptions.3: 4/5 comes from adding 2 to the top and bottom. It is not equal to 2/3.
misconceptions.5: 2/6 keeps the numerator but triples the denominator, so it equals 1/3, not 2/3.

questions.prompt: Write 18/24 in its simplest form.
questions.solution: The highest common factor of 18 and 24 is 6. 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4. So 18/24 = 3/4. (You could also divide by 2 to get 9/12, then by 3 to get 3/4.)

misconceptions.common: Stopping too early, for example at 9/12 after dividing by 2 only. Keep going until the numerator and denominator have no common factor except 1.

questions.prompt: True or false: 15/20 and 9/12 are equivalent fractions.
questions.solution: 15/20: divide both by 5 to get 3/4. 9/12: divide both by 3 to get 3/4. Both simplify to 3/4, so they are equivalent. True.

misconceptions.common: Thinking they are different because the numbers look different. Simplify both fractions first, then compare.

questions.prompt: There are 32 pupils in a class. 12 of them wear glasses. What fraction of the class wear glasses, in its simplest form?
questions.solution: Pupils with glasses: 12 out of 32 = 12/32. The highest common factor of 12 and 32 is 4: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 32 ÷ 4 = 8. So 3/8 of the class wear glasses.

misconceptions.0: 12/32 is correct but not in its simplest form. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 4.
misconceptions.1: 5/8 is the fraction who do NOT wear glasses (20 out of 32). Read the question again.
misconceptions.3: 3/5 = 12/20 compares the pupils with glasses to the pupils without glasses. A fraction of the class compares a part with the WHOLE class of 32.

questions.prompt: A fraction is equivalent to 4/7. Its numerator and denominator add up to 33. What is the fraction?
questions.solution: In 4/7 the numerator and denominator add up to 4 + 7 = 11. 33 ÷ 11 = 3, so multiply both by 3: 4 x 3 = 12 and 7 x 3 = 21. The fraction is 12/21. Check: 12 + 21 = 33, and 12/21 simplifies to 4/7.

misconceptions.common: Adding 11 to both numbers to get 15/18. Its parts add up to 33, but 15/18 simplifies to 5/6, not 4/7. Equivalent fractions come from multiplying both numbers by the same number.

questions.prompt: Which fraction is NOT in its simplest form?
questions.solution: Look for a common factor bigger than 1. 21 and 28 are both in the 7 times table: 21 ÷ 7 = 3 and 28 ÷ 7 = 4, so 21/28 = 3/4. It was not in its simplest form. The other three cannot be simplified.

misconceptions.0: 9 and 16 are not prime numbers, but they share no factor except 1 (9 = 3 x 3 and 16 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2). So 9/16 is already in simplest form.
misconceptions.1: 8 = 2 x 2 x 2 and 15 = 3 x 5 have no common factor except 1, so 8/15 is already in simplest form.
misconceptions.2: 13 is a prime number and does not divide 20, so 13/20 is already in simplest form.

questions.prompt: What is 1/2 written as a percentage?
questions.solution: Percent means 'out of 100'. 1/2 = 50/100 = 50%.

misconceptions.1: You joined the digits 1 and 2. A fraction does not become a percentage by putting its digits together.
misconceptions.2: 1/2 = 0.5 as a decimal, but to make a percentage you multiply by 100: 0.5 x 100 = 50%.
misconceptions.3: The denominator 2 is not the percentage. Make the denominator 100: 1/2 = 50/100 = 50%.

questions.prompt: Write 0.25 as a percentage. Type the number only (for example, type 40 for 40%).
questions.solution: 0.25 is 25 hundredths = 25/100 = 25%. (Or multiply by 100: 0.25 x 100 = 25.)

misconceptions.common: Writing 0.25% or 2.5%. To change a decimal to a percentage, multiply by 100: 0.25 x 100 = 25, so 0.25 = 25%.

questions.prompt: Match each fraction to the decimal with the same value.

misconceptions.common: Thinking 1/4 = 0.4 because of the digit 4. 1/4 means 1 ÷ 4, which is 0.25.

questions.prompt: Which decimal is equal to 3/5?
questions.solution: Make the denominator 10: multiply top and bottom by 2, so 3/5 = 6/10. 6/10 = 0.6.

misconceptions.0: You joined the digits 3 and 5. 3/5 means 3 ÷ 5, which is 0.6.
misconceptions.2: 3.5 is more than 3, but 3/5 is less than 1 because its numerator is smaller than its denominator.
misconceptions.3: Fifths are not tenths. 3/5 = 6/10 = 0.6, not 3/10 = 0.3.

questions.prompt: Write 7/20 as a percentage. Type the number only.
questions.solution: 20 x 5 = 100, so multiply the top and bottom by 5: 7/20 = 35/100 = 35%.

misconceptions.common: Changing the denominator to 100 but not the numerator (giving 7%). Whatever you multiply the bottom by, multiply the top by too: 7 x 5 = 35.

questions.prompt: True or false: 0.4 = 4%.
questions.solution: 0.4 = 4 tenths = 40/100 = 40%. So 0.4 is 40%, not 4%. The statement is false. (4% would be 0.04.)

misconceptions.common: Copying the digit across. Multiply the decimal by 100 to get the percentage: 0.4 x 100 = 40.

questions.prompt: Write 45% as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.solution: 45% = 45/100. The highest common factor of 45 and 100 is 5. 45 ÷ 5 = 9 and 100 ÷ 5 = 20. So 45% = 9/20.

misconceptions.0: You split 45 into the digits 4 and 5. 45% means 45 out of 100, so start with 45/100.
misconceptions.1: Percent means out of 100, not out of 10. 45/10 is 4.5, which is far more than 45%.
misconceptions.3: You divided the numerator by 5 but the denominator by 10. Divide both by the same number: 45 ÷ 5 = 9 and 100 ÷ 5 = 20.

questions.prompt: Select ALL the numbers that are equal to 0.2.

misconceptions.1: 2% = 2/100 = 0.02, which is ten times smaller than 0.2. 0.2 = 20%.
misconceptions.3: 1/2 = 0.5. Perhaps the digit 2 in 0.2 made you think of halves; 0.2 means 2 tenths.

questions.prompt: Write 1/8 as a decimal. Hint: 1/4 = 0.25.

misconceptions.common: Writing 0.8 or 0.18 by using the digit 8. 1/8 is half of 1/4, so it must be smaller than 0.25.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT equal to 3/8?
questions.solution: 1/8 = 0.125, so 3/8 = 3 x 0.125 = 0.375 = 37.5%. 6/16 = 3/8 after dividing by 2. But 0.38 is 0.375 rounded to 2 decimal places: close, but not exactly equal. So 0.38 is the answer.

misconceptions.0: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 exactly (3 x 0.125), so 0.375 IS equal to 3/8.
misconceptions.1: Percentages can have decimals. 0.375 x 100 = 37.5, so 37.5% IS equal to 3/8.
misconceptions.2: 6/16 simplifies to 3/8 (divide top and bottom by 2), so it IS equal to 3/8.

questions.prompt: Look at the large square. It is divided into 100 equal small squares. What percentage of the large square is shaded?

diagram.alt: A large square divided into 100 equal small squares, some of them shaded.

questions.solution: Count the shaded squares: 37 out of 100. Percent means 'out of 100', so 37% is shaded.

misconceptions.1: 63% is the part that is NOT shaded (100 - 37 = 63). Read the question again.
misconceptions.2: 37 out of 100 is 37%. There is no need to move a decimal point.
misconceptions.3: 0.37 is the decimal. As a percentage it is 0.37 x 100 = 37%.

questions.prompt: What is 10% of 60?

misconceptions.0: You multiplied by 10. 10% is 1/10, so you divide by 10.
misconceptions.2: You took 10 away from 60. 10% of 60 means one tenth of 60.
misconceptions.3: You divided by 100. That finds 1%; 10% is 60 ÷ 10.

questions.prompt: What is 50% of 84?

misconceptions.0: You took 50 away from 84. 50% of 84 means half of 84.
misconceptions.1: You doubled 84. 50% is a half, so halve it instead.
misconceptions.3: Place value slip: half of 84 is 42, not 4.2.

questions.prompt: What is 35% of 80?

misconceptions.0: You found 30% (3 x 8 = 24) but forgot to add the 5% (4).
misconceptions.1: Place value slip. Check by estimating: 35% is about one third, and one third of 80 is about 27, so the answer is about 27, not about 3.
misconceptions.2: You took 35 away from 80. 'Percent of' means a part of the amount, not 'take away'.

questions.prompt: What is 1% of RM 450? Give your answer in ringgit.

misconceptions.common: Dividing by 10 instead of 100 gives RM 45, which is 10%, not 1%.

questions.prompt: Look at the rectangle. It is divided into 20 equal parts. What percentage of the rectangle is shaded? Type the number only.
questions.solution: Count the shaded parts: 9 out of 20 parts are shaded, so 9/20. Multiply top and bottom by 5 to make the denominator 100: 9/20 = 45/100 = 45%.

misconceptions.common: Answering 9%. There are 20 parts, not 100, so 9 parts is 9/20, which is 45/100 = 45%.

questions.prompt: True or false: 15% of 60 is 6.
questions.solution: 10% of 60 = 6. 5% is half of that = 3. 15% = 6 + 3 = 9. So 15% of 60 is 9, not 6. False.

misconceptions.common: Stopping at 10%. 6 is only 10% of 60; remember to add the extra 5% (3).

questions.prompt: There are 40 pupils in a hall. 65% of them are girls. How many boys are there?
questions.solution: Boys are 100% - 65% = 35% of the pupils. 10% of 40 = 4, so 30% = 12, and 5% = 2. 35% of 40 = 12 + 2 = 14 boys. Check: girls = 40 - 14 = 26, and 65% of 40 = 26. Correct!

misconceptions.1: 26 is the number of girls (65% of 40). The question asks for the boys.
misconceptions.2: You took 40 away from 65. Find the percentage of boys first (100% - 65% = 35%), then find 35% of 40.
misconceptions.3: 35% is the percentage of boys, not the number of boys. Now work out 35% of 40.

questions.prompt: Mei Lin scored 85% on a test marked out of 60. How many marks did she lose?
questions.solution: She lost 100% - 85% = 15% of the marks. 10% of 60 = 6 and 5% of 60 = 3, so 15% of 60 = 9 marks. (Or: 85% of 60 = 51 marks scored, and 60 - 51 = 9.)

misconceptions.common: Answering 15 (that is the percentage lost, not the marks) or 51 (that is the marks she scored).

questions.prompt: True or false: 40% of 25 is equal to 25% of 40.
questions.solution: 40% of 25: 10% of 25 = 2.5, so 40% = 4 x 2.5 = 10. 25% of 40 = a quarter of 40 = 10. Both are 10, so it is true. (This always works: a% of b = b% of a.)

misconceptions.common: Thinking they must be different because the numbers are swapped. Work out both and compare.

questions.prompt: Which symbol makes this true? 0.7 ___ 0.65
questions.solution: Write both with 2 decimal places: 0.70 and 0.65. 70 hundredths is more than 65 hundredths, so 0.7 > 0.65.

misconceptions.1: 0.65 has more digits, but that does not make it bigger. Compare the tenths first: 7 tenths is more than 6 tenths.
misconceptions.2: They are not equal. 0.7 = 0.70, which is more than 0.65.

questions.prompt: Which is larger: 1/3 or 1/5? Each fraction is shown shaded on a bar of the same length.
questions.solution: Look at the bars. Both bars are the same length. The 1/3 bar is cut into 3 equal pieces, which are bigger than the 5 equal pieces of the 1/5 bar. Both fractions have 1 piece shaded, and the 1/3 piece is longer. So 1/3 > 1/5.

misconceptions.0: 5 is bigger than 3, but a bigger denominator means the whole is cut into MORE pieces, so each piece is SMALLER.
misconceptions.2: Both have numerator 1, but the pieces are different sizes, so they are not equal.

questions.prompt: True or false: 3/4 is less than 70%.
questions.solution: 3/4 = 75/100 = 75%. 75% is more than 70%, so 3/4 is NOT less than 70%. The statement is false.

misconceptions.common: Thinking 70 must be bigger because 70 is a bigger number than 3 or 4. Change both into the same form (percentages) before comparing.

questions.prompt: Put these numbers in order from smallest to largest.

misconceptions.common: Thinking 0.08 is bigger than 0.6 because 8 is bigger than 6. 0.08 has 0 tenths, so it is the smallest.

questions.prompt: Which symbol makes this true? 3/5 ___ 0.35

misconceptions.0: 3/5 is 0.6, not 0.35, and 0.6 is bigger than 0.35.
misconceptions.1: 3/5 is not 0.35. Joining the digits 3 and 5 does not convert a fraction. 3/5 = 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6.

questions.prompt: Which of these is the largest?
questions.solution: Change them all to percentages: 0.7 = 70%, 3/4 = 75%, 72%, 0.69 = 69%. The largest is 75%, which is 3/4.

misconceptions.1: 0.7 = 70%, which is less than 3/4 = 75%.
misconceptions.2: 72 looks like a big number, but 72% = 0.72, which is less than 3/4 = 0.75.
misconceptions.3: 0.69 has more digits, but it is only 69%, the smallest of these.

questions.prompt: Aisha scored 17/20 in Maths, 82% in Science and 0.8 of the marks in English. In which subject did she do best?
questions.solution: Change all three to percentages. Maths: 17/20 = 85/100 = 85%. Science: 82%. English: 0.8 = 80%. 85% is the highest, so she did best in Maths.

misconceptions.0: 82 looks bigger than 17 or 0.8, but you must compare in the same form. Maths is 17/20 = 85%, which beats 82%.
misconceptions.2: 0.8 = 80%, which is the lowest of the three. Maths is 85% and Science is 82%.
misconceptions.3: They are all different: Maths 85%, Science 82%, English 80%.

questions.prompt: Match each comparison to the symbol that makes it true.

misconceptions.common: Thinking 1/3 = 0.3. In fact 1/3 = 0.333..., which is a little more than 0.3.

questions.prompt: The number line shows 0.6 and 70%. Which fraction lies between 0.6 and 70%?
questions.solution: Change everything to percentages: 0.6 = 60%, and the upper end is 70%. 3/5 = 60% (equal, not between). 7/10 = 70% (equal, not between). 3/4 = 75% (too big: past 0.7 on the number line). 2/3 is about 66.7%, which is between 60% and 70%, inside the shaded band.

misconceptions.0: 3/5 = 0.6 exactly, so it is at the end of the range, not between.
misconceptions.1: 7/10 = 70% exactly, so it is at the end of the range, not between.
misconceptions.3: 3/4 = 75%, which is more than 70%.

questions.prompt: Put these numbers in order from largest to smallest.

misconceptions.common: Putting 61% first because 61 is the biggest number you can see, or thinking 5/8 is 0.58. Change everything to decimals before ordering.

questions.prompt: How long is 2.5 hours in hours and minutes?
questions.solution: The 2 is 2 whole hours. The 0.5 means half an hour. Half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes. So 2.5 hours = 2 hours 30 minutes.

misconceptions.0: You read the .5 as 50 minutes. But an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so 0.5 of an hour is half of 60 = 30 minutes.
misconceptions.1: You multiplied 2.5 by 100. There are 60 minutes in an hour, so 2.5 hours = 2.5 x 60 = 150 minutes.
misconceptions.3: You read the digit 5 as 5 minutes. The 5 is 5 tenths of an hour, and 0.5 x 60 = 30 minutes.

questions.skill: converting decimal hours to hours and minutes

questions.prompt: How many minutes are there in 0.75 hours? Give your answer in minutes.
questions.solution: 0.75 is the same as 3/4. One quarter of an hour is 60 / 4 = 15 minutes, so three quarters is 3 x 15 = 45 minutes. Or work it out as 0.75 x 60 = 45.

misconceptions.common: Answering 75 minutes by reading the decimal digits as minutes. An hour has 60 minutes, so multiply by 60: 0.75 x 60 = 45.

questions.prompt: Which shows 1 hour 45 minutes as a decimal number of hours?
questions.solution: 45 minutes is 45 out of 60 minutes, which is 45/60 = 3/4 of an hour. 3/4 = 0.75. So 1 hour 45 minutes = 1.75 hours.

misconceptions.0: You copied the 45 minutes straight after the decimal point. Minutes are sixtieths of an hour, not hundredths, so 45 minutes = 45/60 = 0.75 h.
misconceptions.2: 0.25 h is only a quarter of an hour, which is 15 minutes. 45 minutes is three quarters of an hour, so it is 0.75 h.
misconceptions.3: 1 hour 45 minutes is 105 MINUTES, not 105 hours. To change minutes to hours, divide by 60: 105 / 60 = 1.75 h.

questions.skill: converting hours and minutes to decimal hours

questions.prompt: How many minutes is 0.2 hours?
questions.solution: 0.2 hours means 2 tenths of an hour. One tenth of 60 minutes is 6 minutes, so 2 tenths is 2 x 6 = 12 minutes. Or: 0.2 x 60 = 12.

misconceptions.1: You read 0.2 as 20 minutes, as if an hour had 100 minutes. An hour has 60 minutes, so 0.2 x 60 = 12 minutes.
misconceptions.2: You read the digit 2 as 2 minutes. The 2 means 2 tenths of an hour, and one tenth of an hour is 6 minutes.
misconceptions.3: You worked out 2 x 60 and lost the decimal point. 0.2 is much less than 1 hour, so the answer must be less than 60 minutes.

questions.prompt: True or false: 3.3 hours is the same as 3 hours 30 minutes.
questions.solution: 0.3 hours is 3 tenths of an hour. One tenth of an hour is 6 minutes, so 0.3 h = 3 x 6 = 18 minutes. So 3.3 hours = 3 hours 18 minutes, not 3 hours 30 minutes. The statement is false.

misconceptions.common: Reading the digits after the decimal point as minutes. Hours are split into 60 minutes, not 100, so 0.3 h = 0.3 x 60 = 18 minutes. (3 hours 30 minutes would be 3.5 hours.)

questions.skill: converting decimal hours to hours and minutes

questions.prompt: Write 4.25 hours in hours and minutes.
questions.solution: 4 whole hours stay as 4 hours. 0.25 = 1/4, and a quarter of 60 minutes is 15 minutes. So 4.25 hours = 4 hours 15 minutes.

misconceptions.common: Writing 4 hours 25 minutes. The .25 is a quarter of an hour, which is 15 minutes, because an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

questions.skill: converting decimal hours to hours and minutes

questions.prompt: Write 2 hours 24 minutes as a decimal number of hours. Give your answer as a decimal.
questions.solution: Change the minutes to a fraction of an hour: 24/60. Divide top and bottom by 12 to get 2/5. 2/5 = 0.4. So 2 hours 24 minutes = 2.4 hours.

misconceptions.common: Writing 2.24 hours by putting the minutes after the decimal point. Minutes are sixtieths of an hour, so 24 minutes = 24/60 = 0.4 h.

questions.skill: converting hours and minutes to decimal hours

questions.prompt: A film lasts 96 minutes. How long is that as a decimal number of hours?
questions.solution: Divide by 60 to change minutes to hours: 96 / 60 = 1.6. Check: 1.6 h = 1 hour + 0.6 x 60 minutes = 1 hour 36 minutes = 96 minutes.

misconceptions.0: 96 minutes is 1 hour 36 minutes, but 36 minutes is not 0.36 h. 36 minutes = 36/60 = 0.6 h, so the answer is 1.6 h.
misconceptions.1: You divided by 100 as if an hour had 100 minutes. Divide by 60: 96 / 60 = 1.6 h. (96 minutes is more than 1 hour, so the answer must be more than 1.)
misconceptions.2: You divided by 10 instead of 60. 9.6 hours would be almost 10 hours, far too long for a film of 96 minutes.

questions.prompt: Match each time in decimal hours to the same time in hours and minutes.
questions.solution: Multiply the decimal part by 60. 0.5 x 60 = 30, so 1.5 h = 1 h 30 min. 0.1 x 60 = 6, so 1.1 h = 1 h 6 min. 0.25 x 60 = 15, so 1.25 h = 1 h 15 min. 0.9 x 60 = 54, so 1.9 h = 1 h 54 min.

misconceptions.common: Copying the decimal digits as minutes, for example matching 1.1 h with 1 h 10 min or 1.5 h with 1 h 50 min. Multiply the decimal part by 60 instead.

questions.skill: converting decimal hours to hours and minutes

questions.prompt: Put these lengths of time in order from shortest to longest.
questions.solution: Change them all to minutes. 1.2 hours = 1.2 x 60 = 72 minutes. 75 minutes stays 75. 1.3 hours = 1.3 x 60 = 78 minutes. 1 hour 20 minutes = 60 + 20 = 80 minutes. Shortest to longest: 1.2 hours, 75 minutes, 1.3 hours, 1 hour 20 minutes.

misconceptions.common: Thinking 1.3 hours is 1 hour 30 minutes and putting it last. 0.3 h is only 0.3 x 60 = 18 minutes, so 1.3 hours = 78 minutes.

questions.prompt: Aisha practised the piano for 0.4 hours on Monday and for 1 hour 35 minutes on Tuesday. How long did she practise altogether?
questions.solution: First change 0.4 hours to minutes: 0.4 x 60 = 24 minutes. Then add: 24 minutes + 1 hour 35 minutes = 1 hour 59 minutes. Well done if you changed to the same units first!

misconceptions.0: You took 0.4 hours to be 40 minutes. An hour has 60 minutes, so 0.4 h = 0.4 x 60 = 24 minutes, not 40.
misconceptions.2: You added 0.4 + 1.35, treating 1 hour 35 minutes as 1.35 hours. 35 minutes is not 0.35 h. Change both to minutes before adding.
misconceptions.3: You took 0.4 hours to be 4 minutes. 0.4 is 4 tenths of an hour, and each tenth is 6 minutes, so 0.4 h = 24 minutes.

questions.skill: adding times given in different forms

questions.prompt: Select ALL the lengths of time that are LONGER than 2.4 hours.
questions.solution: Change everything to minutes. 2.4 hours = 2 x 60 + 0.4 x 60 = 120 + 24 = 144 minutes. 2 h 30 min = 150 (longer). 2 h 20 min = 140 (shorter). 145 minutes (longer). 2.35 hours = 120 + 0.35 x 60 = 120 + 21 = 141 (shorter). 2 h 25 min = 145 (longer).

misconceptions.1: 2 h 20 min = 140 minutes, which is less than 2.4 h = 144 minutes.
misconceptions.3: 2.35 hours = 141 minutes, which is less than 144 minutes. Compare 2.35 and 2.40 as decimals: 2.35 is smaller.
misconceptions.common: Thinking 2.4 hours means 2 hours 40 minutes (160 minutes). Then nothing on the list would look longer. 0.4 h is 24 minutes, so 2.4 h = 2 h 24 min.
